newsitem.title: USA: UK 1999 entry into EMU looks hard--Labour's Brown.
newsitem.headline: UK 1999 entry into EMU looks hard--Labour's Brown.

text.p: British entry into European monetary union (EMU) by 1999 looks increasingly difficult, Gordon Brown, economics spokesman for Britain's opposition Labour Party, said on Thursday.
He told reporters that he saw "real hurdles" that make it "increasingly difficult" for British participation in the European single currency at its start in 1999.
But he added that the Labour Party, which has a substantial lead in opinion polls over the ruling Conservatives, still retains the option of joining at that time.

Brown said that every country was looking at "difficulties and hurdles" in meeting the Maastricht treaty requirements for entry into EMU. He set out five additional tests for British participation, including the impact of such a move on investment, Britain's financial services and employment.

Brown accused the ruling Conservatives, who are widely expected to call parliamentary elections in May, of being inconsistent on EMU and said Labour would base its decision on entry on a "hard-headed assessment" of what was in the national interest.
The Labour lawmaker spoke to reporters after a meeting with U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin.
